• The pronoun ‘either’ used in the sentence is incorrect. It means ‘one or the other of two people or things’.

Correct sentence: Vini bought two new dresses but neither of them is suitable for the festival.

questions.solution:

• We have to use the indefinite article ‘a’ before ‘unique responsibility’ since ‘unique’ sounds as if it starts with ‘Y’. ‘A unique responsibility’ means** ‘one unique responsibility’**.

​The other options are cancelled because: 

 
• ‘U’ is a vowel word, but while pronouncing “unique” it sounds as if it starts with ‘Y’ which is not a vowel. So we cannot use 'an'.
 
• 'Some' is used with plural countable nouns and uncountable nouns i.e. if we don't know the exact amount of something or if we use nouns we cannot count, e.g. liquids.
 
• 'Few’ is used to denote a small number of something. It is only used with plural countable nouns.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone __appeared to have been__ switched off.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. No improvement.

 
• The underlined part of the sentence is correct and doesn’t have to be substituted with another phrase.
 
• Look at the given sentence in this way: I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone appeared to have been switched off (by her). This sentence is in the **passive voice**.
 
 
• The **active voice** of this will be: I tried to contact my dentist but she appears to have switched off her cell phone.
 
• The active voice emphasizes the person or agent who performs an action (here it’s the dentist), in short, the “actor.” The **passive voice emphasizes the recipient of the action** or sometimes the action itself (here it’s the **cell phone**).
 
• Eg: Active voice- The dog chased the ball. Passive voice- The ball was chased by the dog.
 
 
 
• The verb tense (have + switched off) when the sentence is in the active voice is **present perfect tense**. 
 
 
• The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time. 
 
• This tense is formed by have/has + the past participle.
 
• In the present perfect tense we make **passive verb forms** by putting has/have + been before the past participle form of the verb. This is what is given in the question- have been + switched off.
 
• Eg: Active voice- I have finished (present perfect) the pudding. Passive voice- The pudding has been finished (passive form of present perfect) by me. 
 
 
 
• The rest of the given options are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

__Be polite and courteous__ will greatly improve your chances of making friends at your new office.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. Being polite and courteous.

The underlined part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect and has to be substituted with another phrase. 

 
• Notice that whatever comes in the underlined part will be the **Subject** in this sentence. 
 
• The subject of a sentence is the person, place, thing, or idea that is doing or being something. You can find the subject of a sentence if you can find the verb. 
 
• Here, ask the question, "Who or what will greatly improve your chances of making friends at your new office?" and the answer to that question is the subject.
 
• ‘Being polite and courteous’ is a gerund phrase acting as the subject. 
 
 
• The gerund looks exactly the same as a present participle, but they are different. To find gerunds in sentences, just look for a verb + ing that is used as a noun.
 
• The gerund always has the same function as a noun (although it looks like a verb).
 
• The gerund phrase can be used as the subject, complement, or object of a sentence. 
 
• Eg: Eating ice cream on a windy day can be a messy experience if you have long, untamed hair. Eating ice cream on a windy day = subject of the verb can be.
 
 

 
• The other options are wrong as they make the sentence grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.**

The vibrations from wind instruments ______ always positive and good ______ your breathing and health.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. are; for. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• According to the **Subject-Verb Agreement rule**, the subject and verb must agree in number. This means both need to be singular or both need to be plural.
 
• **‘The vibrations****’ is a plural subject.** So the verb that accompanies it must be plural too. This helps to cancel out options 1 and 3.
 
• Now option 4 is left. 'Were' is a plural verb but 'to' is the incorrect preposition here. Some instances where 'to' is used are given below:
 
 
• Destination- I’m going to Europe.
 
• Distance- It’s about five miles from my house to the church.
 
• Comparing- I prefer sleeping to exercising.
 
• Giving- He gave the apple to his sister.
 
• Motive- He came here to see you.
 
 
 
• Meanwhile, **‘for’ here is used while stating the benefit of something.** An example of using ‘for’ for this is: *Vitamin C is good for your health. *
 
• Hence we have to use **‘are’(plural verb)** in the first blank and **‘for’(correct preposition)** in the second blank.

**The correct sentence is: ***The vibrations from wind instruments **are** always positive and good **for **your breathing and health.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Chinese leader's formal Chinese suit ______ Changpao.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. is called. 

The sentence can be considered as “The Chinese leader's formal Chinese suit is called Changpao (by someone).” 

 
• This sentence is written in the passive voice.
 
• The passive voice is used when we want to focus attention on the person or thing affected by the action, here the thing is the Chinese suit.

The active voice will be “(Someone) calls(simple present tense) the Chinese leader’s formal suit Changpao.” 

 
• We use the simple present tense for anything that is factual.
 
• When active verb is in the simple present tense (calls), we make passive verb forms with is/am/are + past participle form of the verb (is called). 

​Other options are incorrect because:

 
• Option 1- ​‘Call’ is a base verb and base form of verbs can only be directly used after 

 
 
• modal auxiliaries like can, may, must, would, should, could etc.
 
• Why- eg: Why stay? 
 
 
 
• Option 2- According to the Subject-Verb Agreement rule, the subject and verb must agree in number. This means both need to be singular or both need to be plural.
 
 
• ‘Formal Chinese suit’ is a singular subject. 
 
• So the verb that accompanies it must be singular too. 
 
 
 
• Option 3- ‘Will be called Changpao’ means that the name has not been given to the formal suit yet, and this will happen in the future. This is wrong as this piece of clothing was introduced to China during the Qing dynasty (17th–20th centuries).
